consideredAndDropped: The classic five with a generating and overcoming cycle was dropped (rigid counters). Frost stays the Ice flavour of Water. Wind and Lightning were one element in V2.1 and are now separate (V2.2).
applyRule: V2.2: no wheel, a short nature chart. Enemies are weak (x1.5) or resist (x0.5) by element; a weak hit also triggers a named weakness hit. Reactions between attackers and adjacent allies are removed. Instead, attackers of different elements in the same column fire merges (named pair effects). Element sets at 2 and 4 on the squad are unchanged. Enemies carry the element of their bestiary variant (frost = Water/Ice, storm = Lightning). Flavours add rules but never a new element.

affinityRules.meaning: affinity[attacker][defender] is the damage multiplier of one hit: 1.5 weak, 0.5 resist, 1 neutral. Enemies without an element are x1.
affinityRules.rounding: Weak: ceil(damage x 1.5), so 1 becomes 2, 2 becomes 3, 3 becomes 5. Resist: max(1, ceil(damage x 0.5)), so 1 stays 1, 2 becomes 1, 3 becomes 2, 5 becomes 3. Applied once per hit after buffs, marks and merge bonus damage and before armour. Spread, pierce, chain, echo and Rend hits are each judged on their own element.
affinityRules.weakHit: A weak hit also triggers the named weakness hit once per hit event (area parts once per attack action).
affinityRules.bossesAndElites: Elites and bosses use the same chart as their element. No altered affinities in V2.2. Optional later data field `affinityOverride` ({element: multiplier}) is allowed for at most one entry per boss in region 10, never below x0.5 and never an immunity.
affinityRules.enemyCap: Chilled and similar status effects from weakness hits use the existing caps (Chill -2 total).

mergeRules.scope: Same column of the player board. Attackers need not be adjacent. Rows do not matter except for the carrier.
mergeRules.attacker: A placed card that fires this turn: it has an attack behaviour and ATK >= 1 after boosts. Pure supports, Shields and 0-ATK cards never count. A hybrid (Bastion, Guard plus Attack) counts as one attacker with its single element. Attune and Mimic change the element before merges are read. Classic cards and cards without an element never merge.
mergeRules.pairs: Distinct element pairs among the column attackers fire once each; an element with two or more attackers adds one Resonance for that element. So 3 attackers of 3 elements = 3 merges; A, A, B = Resonance(A) + A+B; A, A, A = one Resonance.

cap.note: 3 is also the natural maximum with 3 attackers in a column. No merge fires twice in a column in one turn.

mergeRules.carrier: The front-most attacker of the pair (nearest the enemies). Resonance: the front-most of that element. The effect rides on the carrier's primary hit; if the carrier cannot strike (Held, no target) the next attacker of the pair carries it, else it is lost. A carrier with two merges gets both on the same hit.
mergeRules.overlap: The same status or effect from two merges on one hit does not stack: the strongest applies. Flat bonus damage from merges on one hit is capped at +2. Area effects (neighbours, jumps) apply once per attack action (B7).
mergeRules.timing: Merges are computed in the Boost phase and shown in the preview; they resolve in the Fire phase on the carrier hit, before armour.

options.name: Own element
options.rule: Each hit is judged by its own attacker's element against the enemy (affinity multiplier and named weakness hit). Merge effects are additional and ride on the carrier hit, which is judged by the carrier's own element.

options.name: Best of column
options.rule: Every hit from an attacker in the column uses the best multiplier among the elements of the column's attackers (x1.5 beats x1 beats x0.5, so a resist applies only when every attacker resists). The named weakness hit comes from the front-most attacker whose element gives the best multiplier, once per hit. Merges are unchanged. A column with one element behaves as Own. No affinity is created for merged elements.

modes.why: Own element keeps every unit's element meaningful and makes the front-line choice matter; Best of column lets one off-element unit carry a whole column and removes the reason to field the right element. Offered as a dev-page switch only.
